title: Interpreting transverse and longitudinal wave graphs

questions.answer: A displacement-distance graph shows the displacements of particles at different positions at one instant. A displacement-time graph shows the displacement of one chosen position at different times.

marking_points.text: Shows that a displacement-distance graph represents different positions at one instant.
Shows that a displacement-time graph represents one chosen position at different times.
Selects C: particle displacement is parallel to energy transfer, so the wave is longitudinal.

option_feedback.A: A graph shape does not determine wave type.
option_feedback.B: Both wave types involve oscillation, so oscillation alone does not classify the wave.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Particle displacement and energy transfer are parallel.
option_feedback.D: Particles oscillate locally rather than moving permanently with the wave.

marking_points.text: Selects B: the graph follows one chosen position at successive times.

option_feedback.B: Correct. A time graph follows one chosen position.
option_feedback.C: A graph records displacement and is not a particle path.
option_feedback.D: Compression positions require a spatial representation, not this one-position time history.

marking_points.text: Selects C: decreasing displacement with distance gives a negative gradient and particle crowding.

option_feedback.A: A positive displacement peak has zero local gradient and is not automatically a compression.
option_feedback.B: A negative displacement peak also has zero local gradient.
option_feedback.C: Correct. A negative gradient shifts neighbouring particles toward one another.
option_feedback.D: A positive gradient spreads neighbouring particles and represents a rarefaction.

parts.answer: The particle at P moves downward. For a right-travelling profile, the portion arriving from the left has a lower displacement because the graph rises at P.

parts.answer: R is a compression and T is a rarefaction. Displacement decreases with distance at R but increases with distance at T.

parts.answer: The sound wave is longitudinal. Air-particle displacement is left and right, parallel to the rightward direction of energy transfer.
parts.unit_policy: Units are required where a numerical quantity is requested; otherwise not applicable.

marking_points.text: Classifies the sound wave as longitudinal.
States that air-particle displacement is parallel to the direction of energy transfer.

parts.answer: U lies at a compression because displacement decreases as distance increases there. Its negative gradient means neighbouring particles move closer together.
parts.unit_policy: Units are required where a numerical quantity is requested; otherwise not applicable.

marking_points.text: Identifies U as the compression.
Links the negative displacement gradient at U to reduced particle spacing.

parts.answer: The vertical graph coordinate records displacement values, not a spatial path. The air particle at V oscillates left and right near one equilibrium position while the wave transfers energy rightward.
parts.unit_policy: Units are required where a numerical quantity is requested; otherwise not applicable.
